newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Eight Palestinians wounded by Israeli gunfire.
newsitem.headline: Eight Palestinians wounded by Israeli gunfire.

text.p: Israeli soldiers firing rubber bullets shot and wounded eight Palestinians on Friday during a seventh day of clashes with Arab stone-throwers in the divided West Bank town, witnesses said.
One youth was shot and seriously wounded in the head.
The witnesses said about 60 Israeli soldiers fired rubber bullets at some 100 youths who rained stones on troops across the invisible line dividing the West Bank town.

The first casualty was a young man who stood next to a demonstrator concealing his face with a chequered black and white Arab headdress and wore the red, white, black and green Palestinian national colours, witnesses said.
They said one soldier aimed at the demonstrator but hit the person standing next to him in the leg. An Israeli army spokeswoman said she was checking the report.
More than 100 Palestinians have been shot and wounded by rubber bullets in six days of violence along the dividing line. Several Israeli soldiers have been hurt.

The clashes erupted over a U.S. congressional vote demanding that the administration recognise Arab East Jerusalem as part of Israel's capital. Witnesses said protesters on Friday burned an American and two Israeli flags.
Palestinians said that unlike previous days, when most of the stone-throwers were children aged between 10-15, many of the demonstrators on Friday were adults.

The clashes underscored tensions over a three-month impasse in Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace moves and Israel's expansion of Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron, the southernmost West Bank city, to Palestinian self-rule in January but kept troops behind to guard some 400 Jewish settlers living or studying in the remaining 20 percent.
